class.name: RayCast3DDirect
class.brief_description: A ray in 3D space, used to find the first object it intersects.
class.description: [admonition type="note" collapsible="true" open="false"] [b]Part of [i]Godot Engine: Conservatory Edition[/i][/b] This is not available in the official build of Godot. [/admonition] A ray in 3D space, used to find the first object it intersects. Unlike its sibling, [RayCast3D], this is not a [Node] and does not go into the scene tree. Instead, you must provide the [RID] for the physics space to query yourself, and then manually invoke the cast. This can be done statically, or through an instance. This can provide its results in a [RayCastResult].

method.name: cast
method.description: Performs a raycast in the provided [param space], updating the state of this object to store the result of the raycast.

method.name: store_in_result
method.description: Copies the current results stored within this object into the provided [param result].

method.name: cast_statically
method.description: A static variation of [method cast] which, provided with a [param space], [param parameters], and [param result] to store the result into, will raycast without requiring a new instance of this type to be created.

method.name: set_transform_and_distance
method.description: A convenience method to setting [member source_position] and [member target_position], which allows setting an origin transform (in world space), and the maximum distance that the ray can travel.

method.name: set_from_parameters
method.description: Edits the state of this object such that the stored settings (such as its exceptions and layers) are identical to that of the provided [param parameters].

method.name: add_exception
method.description: Adds a collision exception so the ray does not report collisions with the specified [CollisionObject3D] node.

method.name: add_exception_rid
method.description: Adds a collision exception so the ray does not report collisions with the specified [RID].

method.name: clear_exceptions
method.description: Removes all collision exceptions for this ray.

method.name: remove_exception
method.description: Removes a collision exception so the ray does report collisions with the specified [CollisionObject3D] node.

method.name: remove_exception_rid
method.description: Removes a collision exception so the ray does report collisions with the specified [RID].

method.name: set_collision_mask_value
method.description: Based on [param value], enables or disables the specified layer in the [member collision_mask], given a [param layer_number] between 1 and 32.

method.name: get_collision_mask_value
method.description: Returns whether or not the [member collision_mask] has its given [param layer_number] set.

members.member: If [code]true[/code], collisions with physics areas (like [Area3D]) will be reported.
If [code]true[/code], collisions with physics bodies (like [PhysicsBody3D]) will be reported.

[b]Only[/b] applies to [ConcavePolygonShape3D] instances (when it has backfaces enabled), and to [HeightMapShape3D] instances. If [code]true[/code], the ray will intersect with faces backwards, for example in heightmap terrain, a ray originating from under the ground will intersect with the ground geometry if shot upward.

[b]Does not apply to[/b] [ConcavePolygonShape3D] instances nor to [HeightMapShape3D] instances, as there is no such thing as an "inside" to these shapes. If [code]true[/code], the ray will detect a hit when starting inside shapes. In this case the collision normal will be [code]Vector3(0, 0, 0)[/code].

The ray's collision mask. Only objects in at least one collision layer enabled in the mask will be detected. See [url=$DOCS_URL/tutorials/physics/physics_introduction.html#collision-layers-and-masks]Collision layers and masks[/url] in the documentation for more information.
The origin, in world space, of this ray. The cast will begin at this point.
The target, in world space, of this ray. The cast will end at this point.
[code]true[/code] if the most recent call to [method cast] collided with something.
If the last ray that was cast (see [member last_hit_something]) was successful, this is the position at which the collision was detected.

If the last ray that was cast (see [member last_hit_something]) was successful, this is the direction of the surface that was hit. If the ray was an interior collision (see [member hit_from_inside]), this will be a zero vector.
If the last ray that was cast (see [member last_hit_something]) was successful, this is the RID of the physics body or area that was hit.

If the last ray that was cast (see [member last_hit_something]) was successful, this is the arbitrary object ID of the physics body or area that was hit. In particular, this is vital to [i]The Conservatory[/i] which uses it to associate collisions with game objects like entities. See [code]ConservatoryObject.GetObject[/code] in C#.

If the last ray that was cast (see [member last_hit_something]) was successful, this is the associated [Object] that was hit. [b]Important:[/b] In [i]The Conservatory[/i] this will be [code]null[/code] for a large amount of objects, simply because they don't actually [i]use[/i] Godot's [Object] type. Prefer using [member last_hit_rid] or [member last_hit_object_id].
If the last ray that was cast (see [member last_hit_something]) was successful, this is the type of physics object that got hit.
If the last ray that was cast (see [member last_hit_something]) was successful, this is the numeric index of the shape within the collider that was hit, or [code]-1[/code] if nothing was hit.

If the last ray that was cast (see [member last_hit_something]) was successful, this is the index of the specific face on the collision object that was hit. This will only ever be set when colliding with a [ConcavePolygonShape3D], and will be set to [code]-1[/code] otherwise. [b]Important:[/b] In [i]The Conservatory[/i], this property won't work unless you use [code]override.cfg[/code] in the game directory to edit [code]physics/jolt_physics_3d/queries/enable_ray_cast_face_index[/code]. Please note that this has a nontrivial memory cost, and is thus not recommended.
